name: yamaha_r1_crossplane
label: Yamaha YZF-R1 998 cc cross-plane inline-four (2009)
based_on: Yamaha YZF-R1 cross-plane inline-four (model code 14B), 2009-2014; 2009 data

sources.what: Yamaha Motor Co. news release of 2008-09-09 for the 2009 European YZF-R1: crossplane description, bore and stroke, compression, power, torque, 4-2-1-2 exhaust. Manufacturer primary source.

totalmotorcycle.com 2009 YZF-R1 page reproducing Yamaha's model feature copy and US/Canada/UK spec tables: firing order 1,3,2,4, intervals, valve sizes, 45 mm throttles, YCC-I switch rpm, exhaust and EXUP. Manufacturer text on a third-party page.
Yamaha 2009 YZF-R1 (Y) service manual on ManualsLib (547 pages): engine specifications pages 39-45, camshaft check page 263, YCC-I feature pages 13-16. Read page by page through text extraction.

Yamaha YZF-R1 racing kit manual on ManualsLib (92 pages, published by Yamaha Motor Engineering, parts prefixed 14B, so the 2009 kit): engine specification table with SBK/STK/STD columns (rev limit, compression, valve timing event angle).
Yamaha YZF-R1 2010 owner's manual (14B-28199-E2) on ManualsLib: tachometer red zone (page 25) and specifications (page 105).
Wikipedia, Crossplane: inline-four crossplane throw sequence and the R1's firing-interval cycle. Encyclopedia page; used only for the explicit pin sequence.
Wikipedia, Yamaha YZF-R1: generation table (alternative 191 hp power figure, 13,750 rpm rev limiter). Used for cross-checking only.

Yamaha 2020 YZF-R1 kit manual (the later 79.0 x 50.9 mm generation, NOT this engine): STD limiter 14500 rpm, compression 13.0, valve timing event angle INT 108 / EXT 110. Read for comparison when choosing the generation; no value above comes from it.

notes: Sourced: bore, stroke, compression ratio, inline-four with crank pins at 0, 90, 270 and 180 degrees, firing order 1-3-2-4 at intervals of 270-180-90-180 degrees, four valves per cylinder, valve diameters 31/25 mm, cam lobe heights and base circles, lobe centres of 105 degrees (a weak reading of the kit manual), 45 mm throttle bodies, 4-2-1-2 exhaust, red zone 13,750 rpm, idle 1200 rpm, published power and torque. Derived from sourced figures, not published as such: valve lift (9.16 mm intake, 8.19 mm exhaust), which is lobe height minus base circle minus mid-range valve clearance. Estimated, not sourced: rod length (110.5 mm); cam duration (248 degrees at 1 mm lift, both cams, centred on the sourced 105 degrees); intake length (0.22 m; the real engine switches between two funnel lengths at about 9400 rpm and the format has one fixed length) and diameter; exhaust primary lengths and diameters, which primaries pair at the 4-2 junction (1 with 4 and 2 with 3 assumed), secondary, silencer and tailpipe dimensions; flywheel inertia; friction_scale 0.6, heat_q 2.7e6 and burn_scale 0.7, the first two at the end of their allowed range. Known gap: about 12% low on torque and 16% low on power. The model's friction rises with the square of engine speed regardless of stroke, which costs a short-stroke engine about 4 bar at 12,500 rpm even at the lowest allowed friction_scale. Not modelled: ram air, the EXUP exhaust valve, the variable intake funnels.

vehicle.name: Yamaha YZF-R1 (2009)
vehicle.notes: European 14B model. curb_kg is Yamaha's wet weight with oil and a full tank (MOTORRAD measured 214 kg; the US bike is listed at 474 lb). final_drive is primary 65:43 x chain 47:17. top_speed_kmh is Yamaha's claim as printed by MOTORRAD. wheel_radius_m is calculated from the tyre size.
